posts.title: Check invoices against orders and agreements
posts.promise: Extract invoice fields, flag mismatches, and leave each decision to a person.
posts.whatItIs: The paid notice describes work handling invoices and checking supporting documents against agreements and orders. A small proposed service could read fictional invoice examples and compare operator-entered fields with a simple agreement/order sheet. The attached workflow example describes extracting invoice details and logging them in a sheet, which supports those prototype mechanics but does not demonstrate agreement matching.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: a professional services office that handles recurring invoices might pay for a reviewed exception queue. The notice establishes a paid human role, not demand for an AI service or willingness to pay.
loop: An operator supplies a fictional invoice and matching test agreement/order row.
The prototype extracts selected fields such as invoice number and amount.
It compares only the fields the operator configured.
It lists missing or differing values with links to the test inputs.
A person checks the documents and decides whether any discrepancy matters.
posts.evidence: The fresh paid notice says the role handles invoices and checks supporting documents against agreements and orders. The n8n listing describes a workflow that extracts invoice details, logs them in a Google Sheet and sends a notification. These sources show the chore and a related example, not this proposed match check or customer outcomes.
posts.uncertainty: This is a proposed fictional-data experiment, not a tested service. Field choices and comparison rules are design choices. The workflow example does not verify agreements or legal/accounting correctness. Real deployment would require permission, access, privacy review and human approval; use fictional records only here.
first24Hours: Create three fictional invoice and order pairs with deliberately varied fields.
Build a sheet with operator-chosen fields and expected values.
Manually compare prototype flags with the examples and record false alerts.
